messages.content: i was reading when someone called my phone. after the call, i could not remember where i stopped.
you could look for the last part you remember clearly. read a little before that place, then go on until you find something new.
i remember the girl in the story going to the market, but not what she bought.
then the part about going to the market gives you a place to begin looking. you may not need to go back to the first page of the whole book.
i found it. i had read one more page than i thought.
now you know where you were. reading a little again helped you find the part that was new to you.
what can i do next time someone calls?
you can put a card between the pages before answering. if there is time, write a word or two about where you stopped.
i do not want to write in the book.
you do not need to. write on the card instead, or just use the card to keep the page.
can you make a short note for me to put by the phone?
keep your page before answering the phone.
my aunt says there was a tree in front of our old house. my father says it was behind the house. i do not know who is right.
you can ask what each person can remember about the place. there may be a picture or another detail that helps. you do not need to choose an answer just because one person sounds more sure.
my aunt says she could see the tree through the kitchen window. my father says the kitchen was at the back.
those details may work together if the tree was behind the house. you could ask your aunt whether she is talking about the back of the house rather than the front.
what if there were two trees?
then both people might be talking about different trees. that is another question to check before choosing one memory as the whole story.
write a simple question for both of them.
could there have been a tree in front and another behind the house?
we found a picture with a tree at the front. does that mean there was no tree behind?
no. a picture of the front may not show the back. it gives information about one part of the house, rather than every part.
write a story where two children make a game while waiting for the rain to stop. use things that are already in a room.

two children sit near a window with a book, a cup, and a card on the table. one asks the other to close her eyes. he moves the card from the book to the cup. when she opens her eyes, she has to say what changed. then they change places. she moves the cup to the other side of the book, and he looks for the difference. they keep playing until the rain stops. then they almost do not want to leave the room.
tell the game in a simple way.
they use a book, a cup, and a card. each person moves one thing while the other has closed eyes. then the other looks for the change. they keep playing until the rain stops.
did they buy a new toy for the game?
no. they used things that were already in the room.
can you add one turn where nobody moves anything?
one child closes her eyes. the other leaves every object in its place. when she looks again, she says that nothing changed. he says that she is right.
why is nothing changed a possible answer?
because there is no rule in that new turn saying that something must move.
my son asked why i was reading a book i had already read. i did not know how to explain it simply.
you could say: i know what happens, but i still enjoy the story. reading it again helps me see things i did not think about before.
give me just those words to say to him.
i know what happens, but i still enjoy the story. reading it again helps me see things i did not think about before.
he says knowing the end should make it no good. what can i say?
you could ask whether he enjoys a song he already knows. knowing the words does not mean he never wants to hear it again. a book can be something a person wants to return to as well.
give me just the question about a song.
do you still enjoy a song when you already know the words?
he says yes. now explain why the book can be like that too.
then you know how something can be good to return to. i enjoy this book even though i know the end.
say my last request simply.
he says yes. now explain why the book can be like that too.
i asked my friend for one book, and they brought three. i only have room for one in my container. help me say that with a kind message.
thank you for bringing these. i only have room for one today. could we choose which one i should take?
that answer is good. i wanted a kind message.
you can thank your friend and still say what you can carry. the request keeps the choice to one book without saying the other books are wrong to bring.
i choose the small one. does that mean it is the book i like most?
not always. you may choose it because you have little space. the reason for choosing a book today may be different from the reason you enjoy it.
explain simply.
you can choose the small book because you have little space. that does not tell us whether it is the story you like most.
write my message after choosing it.
i will take this small book today. thank you for giving me a choice.
can i ask to read another one later?
yes. you could add: could i read one of the other books after i return this one?
my teacher asks what happened in the story and why the child left the room. i wrote only that the child left. did i answer both parts?
no. you said what the child did, but you did not explain why the child left. the question asks for both.
explain that simply.
you said what the child did. you still need to say why the child did it, if the story gives that information.
the child left because someone called from the garden. help me write the answer.
the child left the room because someone called from the garden.
does someone tell us who it was?
no. someone gives us a person without a name. if the story does not say who called, you should not make up a name.
can i answer the question without the name?
yes, if the question only asks why the child left and the story only gives someone calling as the reason. you can keep to what you know without making up a person.
say that last idea simply.
you can answer with what the story says, even when it does not tell you every detail.
i put a clock on my desk today. now i keep looking at it, even when i do not need the time.
you may be looking at it more because it is something new in a place you use often.
say it simply.
you may be looking at it more because it is new on your desk.
i got it from my grandfather. he used to keep it near his books.
then it is new in your room but has a place in your family already. do you like having it near your own books now?
yes. it makes the desk feel less like just a place for work.
you have something there that brings your grandfather to mind. the desk can hold a memory as well as the things you use.
can you write two sentences without saying how i feel?
the clock on my desk came from my grandfather. he used to keep it near his books, and now it is near mine.
what did i ask you to write?
you asked for a short piece about the clock using the facts you gave, without adding a feeling.
write a small conversation at a shop. i want a book for a child, but the worker should ask only one question at a time.

what kind of book are you looking for? a story for a child. does the child read alone or with someone? usually with a parent. would they enjoy a story about animals? yes, i think so. then we can look at these animal stories first.
now make the child like stories about vehicles instead.

what kind of book are you looking for? a story for a child. does the child read alone or with someone? usually with a parent. would they enjoy a story about vehicles? yes, i think so. then we can look at these vehicle stories first.
did i tell you the name of the child?
no. the conversation says that the book is for a child, but it does not give the child a name.
can the worker still help without a name?
yes. the kind of story the child enjoys and how they read can be useful information. a name is not needed for that part.
write a question asking whether the book should be short.
would you like a short story or a longer one?
after lunch, there is some rice left, but no vegetables. can i say there is a whole meal left?
not from that information alone. you know there is some rice, but you do not know whether it is enough for a meal or whether you want other food with it.
i want a note for my brother so he knows what is in the kitchen.
there is some rice left in the kitchen, but no vegetables.
add that he can have the rice if he wants.
there is some rice left in the kitchen, but no vegetables. you can have the rice if you want it.
can i say i made him dinner?
not just from leaving some rice. that might sound like you have made a meal for him. your note can simply say what is really there.
answer without adding anything about what it sounds like.
say that there is some rice. that does not say you made a whole meal.
give me just the note again.
there is some rice left in the kitchen, but no vegetables. you can have the rice if you want it.
i am drawing a card and want to leave room for a message. my friend thinks i forgot to finish the picture.
you can tell them that you are keeping the empty space for words. leaving part of the page empty is part of your plan.
say that simply.
you are keeping the empty space for the message.
give me a message for my friend.
i left that part empty because i want to write a message there.
now help me plan the card. there is a flower on the left, and the words should go on the right.
keep the flower on the left. choose a short message, then write it on the right with enough room around it to read clearly.
i want the words to be thank you for helping me learn.
that is a clear message. you can write it as one line if there is room, or use two lines with thank you on the first and for helping me learn below it.
does changing the number of lines change the message?
no. the words and their order can stay the same even when the writing has more lines.
write a story about two friends who do not walk as fast as each other but still go together.

two friends leave the library for home. one walks fast, and the other stops to look at a garden. the first sees that her friend is far behind and waits near a tree. they choose to walk slowly together so they can talk.
tell the same story in fewer words.
one friend walks fast, then waits for the other. they choose to walk slowly together so they can talk on the way home.
is walking fast always wrong?
no. it was not working for what these two friends wanted to do together. someone walking alone might choose to go fast.
make the story end with both choosing to stop at a garden.
they see a garden with flowers by the road. this time, both stop and look. after a while, they leave together and keep talking on the way home.
did the story say how many minutes the walk took?
no. it says that they walked slowly and stopped, but it does not give a number of minutes.
i told my friend a long story, and they only said i understand. i cannot tell whether they really understood it.
you could ask about one part rather than choosing a reason for the short reply. a short answer can mean different things in different conversations.
what question could i ask without making it a test?
you could say: what did you think about the part where i changed my plan? that asks for their thought about one detail.
i want a kind question rather than a test.
you could ask: was there a part you wanted to hear more about?
what if they say they were tired and did not hear a part?
you can ask which part they want you to tell again. if they need rest, you can also leave the conversation for another time.
write a reply if they did not hear the middle.
would you like me to tell the middle part again, or would another time be better?
does that say i am not happy with them?
no. it gives a choice about talking now or later.
my cousin says i read it when i ask about my message. does that mean she read the book i wrote about too?
no. you asked about your message, so it can be about the message. reading that message does not mean she also read the book it was about.
say it simply.
no. reading your message about a book is not the same as reading the book.
what can i ask if i need to know about the book?
have you read the book too?
she says she only read my message and wants to know if i liked the book. write a reply that says i am still reading.
i am still reading the book, so i do not know what i think of the whole story yet.
i do like the first part. add that.
i like the first part, but i am still reading. i do not know what i think of the whole story yet.
why not say the whole book is good already?
you have only told me that you like the first part. you may want to finish reading before giving a thought about the whole book.
write a story about a parent who wants to read while a baby sleeps, but the baby stops sleeping before she can begin.

a mother puts a book near her chair while her baby sleeps. she makes tea and gets a blanket. just as she sits down, the baby opens his eyes and starts to cry. she puts the book on the table and goes to him. the tea and story wait. later, when the baby is calm, she holds him while telling him about the picture on the first page.
write my request in fewer words.
write about a parent whose reading plan changes when her baby stops sleeping.
make that request simple.
write about a parent who wants to read but needs to be with her baby first.
keep only the first story sentence.
a mother puts a book near her chair while her baby sleeps.
did she read the whole book in the story?
no. she only talked about the picture on the first page.
can that still be a moment with a book?
yes. a person can enjoy looking at a picture and talking about it without reading a whole book.
i have a message ready: we will meet tomorrow at the library. i only need to add after lunch. do not change anything else.
we will meet tomorrow at the library after lunch.
now add that i will bring the book, keeping the first sentence.
we will meet tomorrow at the library after lunch. i will bring the book.
my friend is bringing the book instead. change only that part.
we will meet tomorrow at the library after lunch. my friend will bring the book.
if i send the message to my friend, should it say my friend?
when the message is for your friend, you can use you: we will meet tomorrow at the library after lunch. you will bring the book.
is that asking them to choose, or saying what we already chose?
it says what is already in the plan. it does not ask your friend to choose.
write the whole message without calling it a request.
we will meet tomorrow at the library after lunch. you will bring the book.
can you tell me about the first book you read as a child?
i was not a child and do not have a first book from my own life. i can write a made up story about a child reading a first book.
say it with simple words.
i do not have that memory. i can write a made up story instead.
do that. let the child read with her sister.

a child sits with her sister and opens a small book. at first, she can read only a few words. her sister puts her hand near one line and waits while the child tries. when the child reads the whole line, they smile at each other. the child asks to try the next one too.
keep the last sentence only.
the child asks to try the next one too.
whose memory is that?
it is a made up story, rather than a memory from my own life.
